text:
Alex: FYI seeing a weird tail-latency pattern in eu-west this morning. looks like vGPU allocations are getting interleaved between heavy tenants and tiny bursty ones, causing cold-start chains.
Rachel: ugh. any noisy-neighbor traces?
Alex: short traces attached (summaries below). heuristics show many small jobs getting placed on same GPU slice as long-running batched workers -> kvcache churn + PCIe spikes.
Simon: can you paste the allocation logs?
Alex: here's a sample:```
[2026-03-19T07:12:03Z] alloc tenant=tb-231 slice=vgpu-3 node=rack-22 slot=2 size=0.25
[2026-03-19T07:12:05Z] start tenant=tb-999 job=short-infer seq=1 latency=124ms
[2026-03-19T07:12:05Z] spike node=rack-22 pci_util=98% kvcache_evictions=137
[2026-03-19T07:12:07Z] reclaim tenant=tb-231 cause=preempt
```
Priya: that pci_util=98% line is the smoking gun. looks like vGPU slice sharing isn't respecting nic/egress locality either which amplifies DMA saturation.
Simon: possible mitigations: 1) prewarm small cold pools for short jobs (warm-pool-per-az), 2) soft-affinity by tenant SLO tag to avoid mixing bursty with long-batch, 3) NIC queue shaping at host to reduce DMA tail.
Rachel: prewarm pools -> cost hit. how big? if we keep 50 warm GPUs in eu-west that could be $$$. can we do fractional carveouts instead?
Alex: fractional carveouts help predictable sloting but still share PCIe and kvcache; the expensive part is preventing eviction cascades. prewarm short-run workers on dedicated warm-slice group (smaller vGPU groups pinned to nodes with low batch load).
Priya: quick experiment idea: create a shepherd controller that watches allocation stream and pauses new tiny allocations to any node that has >80% pci_util or >100 kvcache_evictions/1m. throttle window 30s. low-risk, reversible.
Simon: pseudocode for shepherd rule:```yaml
match: allocation.size <= 0.5
reject_if: node.pci_util > 80 || node.kvcache_evictions_1m > 100
backoff: 30s
fallback: route-to=warm-pool
```
Rachel: ^ that seems reasonable as a short-term throttling. we should simulate to estimate request queueing impact and extra latency.
Alex: infra-bot ran a quick sim against yesterday's trace: result -> 12% reduction in max-p99 tail and 0.8% increase in mean lat for bursty tenants, no packet loss.
infra-bot: simulation summary: p99_tail_before=720ms p99_tail_after=635ms mean_burst_before=60ms mean_burst_after=65ms impacted_tenants=24
Priya: great. action items: (1) Simon to land shepherd controller canary in eu-west-canary (2) Rachel to run cost estimate for 3 warm-pool sizes (10/25/50) (3) Alex to add eBPF NIC policing prototype to branch.
Simon: I'll open a PR with canary config. planning 2-hour rolling deploy, monitor pci_util and kvcache_evictions.
Rachel: I'll run the cost model and share numbers by EOD. include committed vs on-demand. include Dedicated-slice delta.
Alex: also flagging this as a candidate for a longer-term routing change: SLO-tag-aware placement + quantized model variants to allow cheaper fallbacks when contention detected.
Priya: yep. we should avoid gating on dedicated pools only — want a routing policy that can gracefully demote to smaller model/quant variant when noisy neighbor detected.
Simon: noted. will add to roadmap backlog after canary.
Rachel: any objections to the shepherd canary timeframe?
Alex: fine with canary today if Simon is comfortable.
Simon: doing it now, posting progress updates. :rocket:
Alex: thanks. ping @oncall if algo causes regression.
infra-bot: alert-channel: #incidents would be notified if p99>800ms for >5m during deployment.
Rachel: tagging this thread for cost review and ops playbook update. :memo:
